note: Track minor-colours, step 3: melodic minor, the raised 6th that closes harmonic minor's gap. Two staffs to tap and compare, natural against melodic minor on a two-scales play-along (pinned to its key, since its backing chord is a chord name), then a line of the student's own over a drone. Every note named is ringed on the staff after it, one extra line per block, and the key is moves with a {{?key}} line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: Melodic minor: the raised 6th and 7th
exercise.why: Harmonic minor leaves a wide gap under its raised 7th, and melodic minor raises the 6th as well to close it, so the scale climbs to the home note by steps.

cells.text:
The first staff below is the {{=key}} harmonic minor scale. Tap {{b6}}, then {{7}}, then {{1}} on it: the first step is wider than any step of a major scale.
The second staff is the {{=key}} melodic minor scale, with {{b6}} raised to {{6}}. Tap {{5}}, {{6}}, {{7}} and {{1}} on it.
Practice until you hear the gap close when you go from the first staff to the second.

Press Play below to start the backing track: one minor chord for eight bars, four in natural minor, then four in melodic minor. Follow the notes view.
Listen for the bar where two notes change: the faded notes are the ones left out, the raised 6th and 7th in the first half and the natural ones in the second.

Press Play below to start the drone. On the staff under it, tap up the scale from the low {{1}}: it is minor up to {{b3}}, and from {{6}} up it is the same as the major scale.
Then tap a line of your own that climbs through {{6}} and {{7}} to {{1}}.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the top of the scale is still the major scale's.
